findings.title: Arbitrary Intent Redirection in WebView2Activity
findings.rationale: The exported activity WebView2Activity retrieves a parcelable extra named 'extra_intent' and passes it directly to startActivity(). An attacker can exploit this by sending an intent to this activity containing a nested intent targeting a non-exported activity (like PrivateActivity or LoginActivity), effectively bypassing component access restrictions.

findings.title: Dynamic Code Loading from Untrusted Packages
findings.rationale: The onLogin method iterates through all installed packages and, if a package name starts with 'com.insecureshopapp', it creates a context for that package with the CONTEXT_INCLUDE_CODE and CONTEXT_IGNORE_SECURITY flags. It then loads and executes code from that package. An attacker can install a malicious app with a matching package name to execute arbitrary code within the context of the InsecureShop application.

findings.title: User Credentials Leaked to System Logs
findings.rationale: The application logs the user's username and password to the system log (Logcat) during the login process. This sensitive information can be read by any application with the READ_LOGS permission (on older Android versions) or by anyone with physical access to the device via ADB.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposed via Implicit Broadcast
findings.rationale: The onSendData method sends a broadcast containing the user's username and password using an implicit intent with the action 'com.insecureshop.action.BROADCAST'. Since no receiver permission or package name is specified, any malicious application on the device can register a receiver for this action and intercept the user's credentials.

findings.title: WebView Universal Access from File URLs Enabled
findings.rationale: The WebView in WebView2Activity is configured with setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true). This setting allows JavaScript running in the context of a file:// URL to access content from any origin, including other local files and remote websites, which can lead to sensitive data theft if a malicious file is loaded.

findings.title: Unvalidated URL Loading in WebView
findings.rationale: WebView2Activity loads URLs directly from intent extras, data strings, or query parameters without any validation. An attacker can use this to force the application to load malicious websites or local files (e.g., file:///data/data/com.insecureshop/databases/...) into the WebView.

findings.title: Application is Debuggable
findings.rationale: The application is marked as debuggable in the manifest. This allows attackers to attach a debugger to the process, inspect the heap, and more easily reverse engineer the application's logic and extract sensitive data.

findings.title: Application Backups Enabled
findings.rationale: The allowBackup attribute is set to true, which allows the application's private data to be backed up via ADB. An attacker with physical access to the device and ADB enabled can extract the application's internal storage, including shared preferences and databases.

findings.title: Cleartext Traffic Permitted
findings.rationale: The application explicitly allows cleartext HTTP traffic. This exposes user data to man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks, where an attacker on the same network can intercept or modify sensitive information transmitted between the app and its backend.

findings.title: Content Provider Protected by Weak Permission
findings.rationale: The InsecureShopProvider is exported and protected by a custom permission with a 'normal' protection level. This means any application installed on the device can request and be automatically granted this permission, allowing unauthorized access to the provider's data.

findings.title: Insecure Broadcast Receiver Starts Activity
findings.rationale: AboutUsActivity registers a CustomReceiver for the action 'com.insecureshop.CUSTOM_INTENT' without specifying any permissions. The receiver takes a 'web_url' from the broadcast and uses it to start WebView2Activity. An attacker can send this broadcast to force the app to open arbitrary URLs.

findings.title: Arbitrary File Leakage via ChooserActivity
findings.rationale: The exported ChooserActivity takes a URI from the EXTRA_STREAM intent extra and copies its content to the external storage. By providing a file:// URI pointing to the application's private internal files, an attacker can trick the app into copying its own sensitive data (like shared preferences) to a world-readable location on the SD card.

findings.title: Hardcoded User Credentials
findings.rationale: The application contains hardcoded credentials for a user 'shopuser'. An attacker can decompile the application to extract these credentials and potentially gain unauthorized access to the user's account or backend services.

findings.title: Hardcoded AWS Identity Pool ID
findings.rationale: The AWS Identity Pool ID is hardcoded in the application's resources. This identifier can be used by an attacker to interact with the application's AWS backend, potentially leading to unauthorized access to cloud resources.

findings.title: WebView TLS Validation Bypass
findings.rationale: The application overrides the `onReceivedSslError` method in its `WebViewClient` and calls `handler.proceed()` for any SSL error. This disables certificate validation, making the application vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks where an attacker can intercept or modify encrypted traffic.

findings.title: WebView Universal Access from File URLs Enabled
findings.rationale: The WebView is configured with `setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true)`, which allows JavaScript running in a file scheme context to access content from any origin, including other local files. This significantly increases the risk of local file theft if an attacker can load a malicious file into the WebView.

findings.title: Unvalidated URL Loading in WebView
findings.rationale: The `WebViewActivity` handles deep links and loads URLs from the `url` query parameter. When the path is `/web`, no validation is performed on the URL. An attacker can use a link like `insecureshop://com.insecureshop/web?url=http://attacker.com` to load arbitrary websites into the app's WebView, facilitating phishing or XSS attacks.

findings.title: Exported Content Provider Leaks Credentials
findings.rationale: The `InsecureShopProvider` is exported and returns the victim's plaintext username and password from SharedPreferences when queried. Although it requires the `com.insecureshop.permission.READ` permission, this permission is defined with a 'normal' protection level, meaning any malicious app on the device can request it and steal the user's credentials.

findings.title: FileProvider Configured with Root Path Access
findings.rationale: The FileProvider configuration includes a `<root-path>` element mapping to the device's root directory (`/`). This is a dangerous configuration that allows access to any file on the device if the application grants URI permissions for a path under this provider to an external entity.

findings.title: Cleartext Traffic Permitted
findings.rationale: The application explicitly permits cleartext HTTP traffic. This allows an attacker on the same network to intercept sensitive data transmitted by the app using Man-in-the-Middle techniques.

findings.title: Plaintext Password Storage
findings.rationale: The application stores the user's password in plaintext within SharedPreferences. This data is vulnerable to theft on rooted devices or through ADB backups, as the application also has the `allowBackup` flag enabled.
